text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
Robusta futures in London closed lower overwhelmed by selling orders from the origins. March closed $20 lower at $1,678 per tonne, while May gave up $41 to close at $1,657 per tonne.

The market will keep a watch on Thursday's Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) technical group meeting in London although no major decision is expected. The meeting is expected to analyze the recent sharp rise in world market prices and its impact on consumption. The technical group is made up of Brazil, Colombia, Indonesia, Ivory Coast, El Salvador and Uganda. Arabica futures in New York closed lower after the market lost interest in news of a potential port strike in Colombia, which had pushed up prices initially. The CSCE reported late Wednesday certified coffee stocks grew for the tenth day in a row, reaching 64,529 60-kg bags as of March 18. There were an additional 17,100 bags pending grading, the exchange said. May and July lost 70 points to close at 168.10 and 154.90 cents/lb respectively. Traders believe that the market may remain under pressure from increased exports the next few weeks, but that thereafter the situation will become tight once again.

HONDURAS - Honduras exported 347,884 60-kg bags of green coffee in February, the Honduran Coffee Institute said. February's exports were higher than those of recent months, in part because of an increased interest in exporters to ship and in part a reflection of the harvest peak. The Honduran statistics do not include Nicaraguan coffee exported through Honduran ports but do include Honduran coffee loaded at Guatemalan ports, traders said.

COLOMBIA - Dock workers at Buenaventura, Colombia's main Pacific Coast port and the shipment point of 60 per cent of the country's coffee exports, are threatening new strike action, a union official said. The strike, which could begin in less than a month if no deals are reached, is being threatened in protest at port operators' failure to fulfill the terms of an accord hammered out in January, which ended a crippling nine-day work stoppage.

IRELAND - Ireland imported 96,500 bags of coffee in January/October 1996, slightly less than the 97,100 bags imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 15 per cent to 114,900 bags. Ireland gets most of its coffee in the form of solubles from the United Kingdom.

SOUTH KOREA - South Korea imported 818,300 bags of coffee in January/October 1996, 9 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 7.5 per cent to 1.084 mn bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Honduras (122,900 vs 87,700 bags), Colombia (103,700 vs 109,400 bags), Indonesia (168,200 vs 56,200 bags) and Thailand (99,900 vs 140,400 bags).
